rationale: The latest observed PM2.5 is the natural anchor of a next-hour forecast (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.96 in training).

features: hour_sin, hour_cos, dow_sin, dow_cos, month_sin, month_cos, is_weekend
rationale: PM2.5 shows a daily cycle (night maximum, afternoon minimum), a seasonal cycle (Oct-Dec high, Aug low) and a small weekend effect in the training EDA; cyclical sin/cos encodings avoid artificial jumps at midnight / year end.

features: PM25_lag_1, PM25_lag_3, PM25_lag_6, PM25_lag_12, PM25_lag_24, PM25_lag_48, PM25_lag_168
rationale: Concentrations persist over hours (1-6 h), days (24 / 48 h) and weeks (168 h); individual lags capture specific recurrences.

features: PM25_roll_mean_3, PM25_roll_mean_6, PM25_roll_mean_12, PM25_roll_mean_24, PM25_roll_std_6, PM25_roll_std_24
rationale: Means and standard deviations of the shifted series (window ends at t-1) summarise recent level and volatility and average out single noisy readings.
Co-pollutants share sources and meteorology with PM2.5 (PM10 and CO are strongly correlated with the target in the training EDA).

features: TEMP, PRES, RAIN, WSPM, wd (15 one-hot dummies, reference N)
rationale: Wind speed/direction ventilate the air; precipitation scavenges particles; pressure and temperature mark stagnation. Wind direction is one-hot encoded (no artificial ordering); DEWP enters through TEMP-DEWP.
Physically motivated quantities that passed the training-only EDA rule (|Spearman| >= 0.10 with the target or the next-hour change): moisture and aerosol-composition indicators.

features: TEMP_x_DEWP, TEMP_x_PM10, WSPM_x_PM10, WSPM_x_PM25, TEMP_x_hour_sin, DEWP_x_hour_sin
rationale: Context-dependent effects: ventilation x load, temperature x moisture, seasonal composition, diurnal modulation. Inputs are mean-centred inside each training fold to limit artificial collinearity.
